catalog_locator: sec. 3.2 para <39>-<40> (loss of tonemic tone); sec. 3.3 para <41> (phonology: de-prenasalization only)
catalog_quote: 3.2. Loss of the meaning-distinguishing function of tone <39> The evidence shows that the language did not make use of tone distinctions at a tonemic, i.e. meaning-distinguishing, level, neither in the lexicon nor in the grammar. It did fulfill such meaning-distinctive roles in original Bobangi. This functional load of tone was lost during pidginization. (After 1900, during the phases of expansion/extension, Lingala regained meaning-distinguishing tone under the influence of adstrates; but these post-1900 processes of regain lie outside the scope of my contribution.) <40> Loss or reduction of the functional load of tone has often been mentioned in pidginization studies worldwide ... 3.3. Phonology <41> To be noticed is the de-prenasalization of word-initial unvoiced consonants. For instance, in Bobangi, the word for 'goat' was ntaba, while in the pidgin this became taba.

sources.locator: Ch. I, sec. D 'On Accents', p. 4
sources.note: downloaded now: p. 4 gives an explicit accent rule (primary accent on first stem syllable, secondary on penult in words of >3 syllables). It should be entered as a caution/secondary note on this record, flagged that Meeuwis 2020 <34> excludes Stapleton's books as missionary-'corrected' Bangala, so it is not clean evidence for the pidgin (arguably belongs with early Lingala ling1263 / Bangala bang1353).
